title: Input
lead: Input allows the user to enter and edit text.

examples.name: Appearance
examples.description:
An input can have different appearances.
The colors adjacent to the input should have a sufficient contrast. Particularly, the color of input with
      filled darker and lighter styles needs to provide greater than 3 to 1 contrast ratio against the immediate
      surrounding color to pass accessibility requirements.

examples.name: Content before/after
examples.description: An input can have elements such as an icon or a button before or after the entered text. These elements are displayed inside the input border.

examples.name: Inline
examples.description: An input can be rendered inline with text.

examples.name: Placeholder
examples.description: An input can have placeholder text. If using the placeholder as a label (which is not recommended for usability), be sure to provide an `aria-label` for screen reader users.

examples.name: Size
examples.description: An input can have different sizes.

examples.name: Type
examples.description:
An input can have a custom text-based [type](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/HTML/Element/Input#input_types) such as `email`, `url`, or `password` based on the type of value the user will enter.

Note that no custom styling is currently applied for alternative types, and some types may activate browser-default styling which does not match the Fluent design language.

examples.name: Uncontrolled
examples.description: By default, an input is uncontrolled: it tracks all updates internally. You can optionally provide a default value.

examples.name: Controlled
examples.description: An input can be controlled: the consuming component tracks the input's value in its state and manually handles all updates.

prose.text:
## Best practices

### Do

- **Consider using `Input` with underline or outline appearances.** When the contrast ratio against the immediate surrounding color is less than 3:1, consider using underline or outline styles which has a bottom border stroke. But please ensure the color of bottom border stroke has a sufficient contrast which is greater than 3 to 1 against the immediate surrounding.

### Don't

- **Don't place input on a surface which doesn't have a sufficient contrast.** The colors adjacent to the input should have a sufficient contrast. Particularly, the color of input with filled darker and lighter styles needs to provide greater than 3 to 1 contrast ratio against the immediate surrounding color to pass accessibility requirements.

tables.name: Input
rows: Wrapper element which visually appears to be the input and is used for borders, focus styling, etc. (A wrapper is needed to properly position `contentBefore` and `contentAfter` relative to `input`.) The root slot receives the `className` and `style` specified directly on the `<Input>`. All other top-level native props will be applied to the primary slot, `input`.

The actual `<input>` element. `type="text"` will be automatically applied unless overridden. This is the "primary" slot, so native props specified directly on the `<Input>` will go here (except `className` and `style`, which go to the `root` slot). The top-level `ref` will also go here.
Element before the input text, within the input border
Element after the input text, within the input border
Size of the input (changes the font size and spacing).
'outline' Note: 'filled-darker-shadow' and 'filled-lighter-shadow' are deprecated and will be removed in the future.
Controls the colors and borders of the input.

Default value of the input. Provide this if the input should be an uncontrolled component which tracks its current state internally; otherwise, use `value`. (This prop is mutually exclusive with `value`.)

Current value of the input. Provide this if the input is a controlled component where you are maintaining its current state; otherwise, use `defaultValue`. (This prop is mutually exclusive with `defaultValue`.)
Called when the user changes the input's value.

An input can have different text-based [types](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/HTML/Element/Input#input_types) based on the type of value the user will enter. Note that no custom styling is currently applied for alternative types, and some types may activate browser-default styling which does not match the Fluent design language. (For non-text-based types such as `button` or `checkbox`, use the appropriate component or an `<input>` element instead.)
